newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-Australian lab stands by Busang gold grade.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Australian lab stands by Busang gold grade.

text.p: An Australian company which tested the original assay samples from the Busang gold site in Indonesia said on Tuesday that the samples had been of good grades indicating a major deposit.

Shares in Canadian miner Bre-X Minerals plummeted last month when its U.S. partner in the Busang exploration said the property -- once touted as the world's largest orebody -- might contain "insignificant" amounts of gold.

But Phil Hearse, a director at metallurgical consultant Normet, denied Canadian press reports that the assay samples it tested last July contained placer or alluvial gold, usually found in streams or rivers, rather than bedrock gold.
"We have never reported placer gold as being part of Busang," Hearse told Reuters from the west Australian city of Perth. "That is incorrect. Absolutely."
"We reported the shape of some particles that we found and another paper picked that up and basically said we said they were placer particles and that's totally incorrect," he said.
Asked whether the Busang assay samples had indicated a major deposit, Hearse replied: "They certainly did. (The samples) indicated good grades of gold."
The samples, provided by Bre-X, were sent to Normet last year from Balikpapan, the nearest town to the Busang orebody on Kalimantan.
Hearse's statements, the latest twist in the Busang saga, mean that billions of dollars invested in the Canadian miner continue to hang in the balance.

Reacting to his comments, analysts queried why Bre-X had never announced Normet's assay test results to the market and said there was still a contradiction with the declarations of Bre-X's U.S. partner Freeport.

From reserves once said to amount to 70.95 million ounces, it appeared that there may be virtually no gold in Busang when Freeport-McCoRan Copper & Gold Inc said last month that drilling tests indicated the deposit may contain only "insignificant" amounts of gold.
Bre-X shares, which had soared in value on the Busang find, collapsed on March 27, wiping nearly C$3 billion off the value of the mining junior.
Bre-X has asked for further tests to be done on ore samples, by Canadian consultant Strathcona Mineral Services Ltd. The testing will be done in Perth.
Hearse said the samples for Strathcona had not yet arrived in Perth and he was not at liberty to say when they would.

Hearse said he would not estimate tonnages in Busang but he stood by initial interpretations of good grades in samples sent to Normet from Balikpapan --- "(which) to our knowledge were from the Busang hardrock deposit".
"Then you have to couple that with the number of tonnes in the deposit which is not within our scope," he said.
